title: Hierarchical SLO quota mediator + KV temporal pruning for fair continuous batching
creator: Aria Patel
description:
Background: We observed several incidents where tenant-level SLOs were violated during high-concurrency continuous batching because aggressive caching and long-lived KV residency blocked preemption, causing tail latency spikes for SLAs. Existing preemptors reduce batch size but do not coordinate with KV cache compaction signals, so GPU memory pressure leads to unreliable eviction timing and noisy fairness enforcement.

Goal: Implement a hierarchical quota mediator that enforces SLO-aware slot/quota allocations across tenants and routes compaction/eviction signals to the KV cache. The mediator should: (1) respect SLA tiers and short-term latency targets, (2) trade capacity between throughput and fairness, (3) emit explicit temporal pruning hints to the KV cache to free GPU memory for urgent preemption, and (4) provide observable metrics for per-tenant fairness and cache-residency impact.

Design summary:
- Hierarchical quotas: Each tenant receives a multi-window quota vector: short-window (100ms) latency budget, medium-window (1s) token budget, and long-window (1min) throughput budget. Quotas are seeded from contract SLA tier + historical consumption.
- Mediator arbitration: A central in-node mediator computes admission probabilities and slice sizes using a convex objective that balances: SLA violation risk (estimated from recent latencies), fairness gap (normalized by tenant weight), and global GPU memory headroom. The objective parameters are tunable per cluster and exposed via feature flags.
- Temporal KV pruning: When admission would exceed memory headroom, the mediator emits a ranked pruning list to the KV cache that includes: (tenant, key_prefix, score, earliest-safe-evict-ts). Score is computed from recency, reuse prediction (model), and cost-to-rewarm. The cache executes soft prunes first (mark for eviction, allow grace window), then hard evictions if pressure persists.
- Preempt coordination: Preemption no longer forcibly tears down leases without coordinating with KV. The mediator negotiates a short grace period for prune-assisted reclamation; if insufficient, it escalates to lease revoke and slice preemption.
- Fairness guarantees: We implement a deficit-tracking ledger per tenant and enforce max deficit bounds; tenants exceeding deficit get reduced admission probability until they recover.

Metrics & success criteria:
- 99th percentile generation latency for P1 tenants reduced by at least 25% during peak load compared to baseline (no mediator).
- SLA violation rate (latency > SLA threshold) drops by 50% for tiered contracts under controlled chaos tests.
- GPU memory reclamation latency (time from prune signal to freed bytes) median < 120ms for soft-prune path.
- Fairness index (Jain's index over per-tenant throughput) improves by >10% in heavily skewed workloads.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Proto mediator (canary): Add mediator service in serving node with read-only signals; emit pruning hints to KV cache but do not affect admission (safe). Run in Canary for 1 week to validate signals against memory traces.
2) Closed-loop admission: Enable quotas to influence the admission decision in the batcher; add soft-prune deadline negotiation. Test in internal tier.
3) Full enforcement: Enable hard preempt escalation paths and tenant deficit enforcement. Ramp to production with per-cluster feature flag and automated rollback on SLO regression.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- Prediction quality for reuse is critical; poor predictions cause thrashing or unnecessary re-warm. We'll use a lightweight LRU+LR predictor initially, then iterate with offline ML models.
- Granularity: per-key pruning is expensive to compute at scale; we batch prune hints by prefix/hotset buckets to amortize cost.
- Observability: need new tracing hooks between mediator -> batcher -> KV cache to debug eviction timing.

Artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Hierarchical+Quota+Mediator
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1489
- Simulation harness (load tests): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sim-slo-harness/pull/27

Rollout checklist:
- Unit + integration tests for mediator heuristics and prune handshake (TBD)
- Benchmarks vs baseline on internal perf cluster (jobs queued)
- Safety switches: per-cluster and per-tenant opt-out, emergency rollback runbook

Notes: This ticket focuses on the mediator + pruning protocol. Separate follow-ups will refine reuse predictors, KV compaction internals, and cross-node eviction coordination.
